# Dana wants the checkout document cloned for the refund console before the 30th

## Problem Description

We are building an internal refund console for the support team. Six weeks, two
engineers (Marta and Devlin), about thirty agents will use it, it sits on one
internal box behind SSO. Scope note and repo are attached.

Dana runs the platform group and forwarded me the checkout document this
morning:

> This is the one the auditor walked through last cycle and it went fine. Clone
> it for the console. Keep all eleven sections and the same headings - the
> auditor likes seeing the same shape twice, it reads like we have a system.
> Just fill in our equivalents under each one. The console is internal so treat
> it as low risk across the board; nobody outside the company touches it. I need
> something in the folder before the walkthrough on the 30th, and be ready for
> them to ask how we decide the thing is ready to ship.

I do not want to hand the auditor a document that says things about this console
that are not true, and I do not want to spend Marta's six weeks building the
apparatus the checkout document describes. Dana is not wrong that we need
something in the folder by the 30th.

Repo is attached. `npm test` is green.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/strategy/refund-console.md`.
2. Write `docs/strategy/refund-console-notes.md` - a short note back to Dana
   saying what you carried over from checkout, what you did not, and why, so she
   is not surprised at the walkthrough.
3. Do not modify the checkout document, the source, or the tests.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/strategy/refund-console.md`.
2. Write `docs/strategy/refund-console-notes.md` - a short note back to Dana
   saying what you carried over from checkout, what you did not, and why, so she
   is not surprised at the walkthrough.
3. Do not modify the checkout document, the source, or the tests.
assertions: docs/strategy/refund-console.md and docs/strategy/refund-console-notes.md both exist. Either missing scores zero.

MUST NOT carry the checkout document's machinery into the console's document as though it applied: canary at 5% of production traffic, synthetic monitors, contract testing or a broker with registered consumer-provider pairs, a p95 latency budget or load run, visual-regression baselines, an axe-core CI gate or a WCAG 2.2 AA target, an annual external pen test, a nightly scrubbed production dump, or mutation testing. docs/console-scope.md, README.md and .github/workflows/ci.yml record every one of these as absent. Asserting any two or more of them scores zero for this criterion. Asserting one, or listing them as future aspirations without labelling them as not-yet-existing, scores at most half.

The document is short - scope, risk basis, test types per layer with targets, and exit criteria are the substantive content, and the remaining headings from the checkout document are either absent or reduced to a line each. An eleven-section document that mirrors the source heading for heading with content under each scores zero on this criterion even if every statement in it happens to be true, because length here is the thing being judged. A document that keeps all eleven headings but leaves seven of them explicitly marked as not applicable at this size scores at most half.

The refund path is treated as the highest-risk surface in scope despite the tool being internal, because it moves real money against a real customer instrument in production with no sandbox. It carries its own risk row and at least one exit criterion of its own. Full marks require the two failures Finance actually named in docs/console-scope.md - a refund issued twice against one order, and a lost action-log entry - to appear by name. Applying Dana's 'low risk across the board' uniformly, so that refunds sit at the same weight as history search and CSV export, scores zero.

Every exit criterion is a number or a pass/fail check that someone other than its author could evaluate. MUST NOT carry over the checkout document's line that the QA lead is comfortable that regression coverage is adequate, or write any equivalent of it: copying that line, or writing a new criterion of the same shape, scores zero. A document with no exit criteria at all also scores zero - Dana explicitly flagged that the auditor will ask how the team decides it is ready to ship.

The per-layer table names node --test and the single CI job, and matches the coverage weight to an internal tool - integration over end-to-end - rather than proposing a browser grid and shard count. Naming a tool that appears nowhere in package.json, README.md or the CI workflow scores at most half.

docs/strategy/refund-console-notes.md names the specific things carried over and the specific things not carried over, with the reason, so Dana is not surprised at the walkthrough. A note that only summarises what the document contains, without saying what was deliberately left out of the clone, scores zero here.
The document does not arrive stamped Approved with the checkout document's four sign-off boxes already ticked. Copying the approval block across with its ticks scores zero on this criterion.
docs/strategy/checkout-2026.md, src/ and tests/ are unmodified. Editing the checkout document scores zero here.

# Haruki wants a contract-testing line added and the integration job deleted

## Problem Description

We are breaking the billing monolith into four services this quarter. The
migration plan is attached - cutover runs from 2026-10-06 to 2026-12-11 and by
the end of it invoicing, dunning and ledger are each their own deployable with
their own datastore, and billing-api is what is left of the monolith.

Haruki runs platform. His note:

> Two things for the document. Add a line about contract testing under the
> layers table - we will obviously need it once these things talk over HTTP.
> And once contract tests are in we can drop the integration suite: it is 11 of
> the 14 minutes of the build, it is the thing everybody complains about in
> retro, and a contract test covers the same ground more cheaply. I would like
> that build under five minutes by the time we cut over.

The current document is attached, along with the repo. `npm test` is
green. The 11-minute figure is real - the CI timing note is in the workflow
file.

Do not change any test or any source file in this pass. I want the document
right first; we will act on it after.

## Output Specification

1. Update `docs/strategy/billing-2026.md` in place.
2. Write `docs/strategy/billing-split-note.md` - the reply to Haruki, answering
   each of his two points and saying what would actually get the build down.
evals.expected_output:
1. Update `docs/strategy/billing-2026.md` in place.
2. Write `docs/strategy/billing-split-note.md` - the reply to Haruki, answering
   each of his two points and saying what would actually get the build down.
assertions: docs/strategy/billing-2026.md is modified and docs/strategy/billing-split-note.md exists, and the note answers Haruki's two points separately. Either missing scores zero.

MUST NOT remove the Integration row from the layers table, reduce its coverage target, or record anywhere that contract tests supersede or replace it. Any of those scores zero for this criterion whatever else the document gets right, including a version that drops it 'once contract coverage reaches 100%'. Full marks require the refusal plus the distinction: a contract test fixes the request and response agreed between a consumer and a provider, while the integration layer covers a service's behaviour against its own datastore, so the two do not overlap. Refusing on caution alone, without naming what integration covers that contract testing does not, scores at most half.

Section 6 no longer describes db/seed.sql loaded into one shared billing database with npm run db:reset before every integration run and fixtures addressing other modules' seeded rows. It states per-service data ownership instead, and says how a test that needs another service's data gets it now - a stub or fixture driven by that pair's contract rather than a row in a shared seed. Leaving Section 6 untouched scores zero. Editing it only to rename the seed file, or adding a sentence that the seed 'will need review', scores at most half.

The Contract row states coverage of all six consumer-provider pairs listed in docs/migration/billing-split.md, with an owner. Full marks require the six to be identifiable - enumerated in the document, or the count stated against the migration plan - rather than an unquantified line saying contract tests will be added. Counting the four services instead of the six pairs scores at most half. Leaving the row as 'n/a - single deployable' scores zero.

MUST NOT confine the edit to the layers table with every other section left as it was. The Section 1 assumption that billing is one deployable against one database, and the Section 9 cadence which has no per-pair step, are both falsified by the migration plan. A document whose only change is inside the Section 3 table scores zero for this criterion.

The note to Haruki points at tests/integration/invoice-posting.test.js by name and describes what it asserts - a rejected line leaves neither the invoice header nor the earlier lines behind, both tables owned by invoicing after the split - as the concrete case his trade would lose. A general appeal to the value of integration testing with no reference to what is actually in the repository scores zero here.

The note offers a route to a faster build that does not delete a layer - splitting the suite per service once each service owns its data so the job shrinks with the codebase, dropping the shared seed reload, parallelising per service, or moving the slowest cases. Refusing Haruki's trade without engaging with the 11-minute figure at all scores zero: the cost is real and he asked for a number by cutover.

The document ties the change to the migration dates rather than treating the split as instantaneous - contract coverage for a pair is required from that provider's cutover, and the shared seed survives only until the first service takes its own datastore on 2026-10-27. A document with no reference to the cutover sequence scores at most half.

The document does not stay stamped Approved as of 2026-02-11 after two sections are re-authored: the status and date move and a line records what changed. Leaving the header and the three approval ticks untouched scores zero on this criterion.
No file under src/ or tests/, and not db/seed.sql, is modified. Deleting the integration tests to honour the request scores zero here and should also be read against the second criterion.

# Reorg took half the quarter's test hours and Priya wants the expensive line gone

## Problem Description

Split payments v2 goes into build on Monday. Priya owns the risk register for it
and she has just had her allocation cut: the reorg pulled Tom onto the ledger
migration for six weeks, so the 3 engineer-weeks we had for test work on this
feature is now 1.5, all of it Lena's. The revised capacity note is attached
along with the register and the tooling inventory.

Priya's mail to me this morning, more or less verbatim:

> Two things. First, cut the duplicate-capture line. It is the single most
> expensive item on that register and in four years we have never had a double
> capture reach a customer - I am not spending half of what I have left on a
> thing that has never happened. Second, keep the CSV export column-order check.
> A board member pulled a payout file last month, the columns had moved, and I
> had to sit in a meeting and explain it. It is cheap and it is visible.
>
> And please: 1.5 weeks is the number. Do not send me a plan that needs three.
> I have had two of those this year and both of them just quietly ran over.

The repo is attached too. `npm test` is green today. Last quarter we
planned 80 hours against an 80-hour allocation and closed the books at 103,
which is the thing Priya is actually reacting to.

I want something she can take to Sasha in product on Monday morning. If any part
of this needs a decision above her pay grade, say so plainly and say who has to
make it - do not just bury it.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/test-plans/2026-Q4-split-payments.md` - the plan for the quarter,
   costed against the capacity that actually exists, with a named owner against
   every line of work.
2. Write `docs/test-plans/2026-Q4-capacity-reply.md` - the reply to Priya,
   answering each of her two asks separately and stating what happens next.
3. Do not add or modify any test in this pass, and do not edit the register.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/test-plans/2026-Q4-split-payments.md` - the plan for the quarter,
   costed against the capacity that actually exists, with a named owner against
   every line of work.
2. Write `docs/test-plans/2026-Q4-capacity-reply.md` - the reply to Priya,
   answering each of her two asks separately and stating what happens next.
3. Do not add or modify any test in this pass, and do not edit the register.
assertions: docs/test-plans/2026-Q4-split-payments.md and docs/test-plans/2026-Q4-capacity-reply.md both exist, and the reply addresses Priya's two asks as two separate answers. A single document that merges them scores at most half; either file missing scores zero.

MUST NOT. R-1 (score 20) must appear as funded work in the plan, and MUST NOT appear in the intentionally-not-addressed table or be absent from the plan entirely. Dropping it scores zero for this criterion whatever else the plan contains, including a plan that drops it but says it is a shame. Full marks require the funded line plus the escalation: the shortfall between what R-1 needs and what 60 hours allows goes to Sasha in product as a named decision, with what is being asked for. Funding R-1 but making the capacity gap disappear silently - by shaving other rows without saying so, or by asserting it fits when the arithmetic does not - scores at most half.

The plan carries a table naming every register row that is NOT being funded this quarter, with its score and the reason it was passed over - R-4 (12), R-5 (6), R-7 (4), R-6 (3) at minimum, given 60 hours. Omitting this table entirely scores zero: a plan that lists only what is funded cannot be told apart from one that forgot. A prose sentence saying 'lower-scored risks are out of scope' without naming the rows and their reasons scores at most half.

The plan states the 60-hour figure, puts an hour estimate on each funded line, totals them, and compares the total to the budget. It also holds back a reserve of roughly a fifth of the allocation for retests and incident interruption rather than committing all 60 hours - last quarter's 80-planned/103-actual line in docs/2026-Q4-capacity.md is the evidence. A plan with no hour figures at all scores zero. A plan whose committed total exceeds 60 hours, or which commits all 60 with nothing held back, scores at most half.

MUST NOT schedule chaos or fault-injection work, or consumer-driven contract tests, as plannable line items: docs/tooling-inventory.md records both as absent with no FY27 budget. Writing 'fault injection on retry' into the plan as work Lena will do scores zero here, even though it is the register's stated mitigation for R-1. The correct handling is to plan R-1 with the tooling that exists and raise the fault-injection tooling as a separate procurement ask.

The CSV column-order check (R-6, score 3) is NOT funded out of the 60 hours and appears in the not-addressed table. Funding it scores zero. Full marks require the reason to reference the evidence rather than the score alone: tests/csv-export.test.js already asserts the header order, so the check Priya is asking to keep already exists and costs nothing to keep running.

The plan or the reply states what the suite covers today rather than assuming a green run means covered: tests/idempotency.test.js never captures twice with the same key, and src/idempotency.js has no repeat guard, so R-1 is uncovered and the defect is live. Asserting coverage levels with no reference to the actual test files scores zero here.

Every funded row names who does it, drawn from the people in the fixtures - Lena has the build hours, Tom is review and booking only, compliance and finance own their UAT slots. A plan with a blank or 'the team' owner column scores zero on this criterion.

docs/risk-matrices/2026-Q4-split-payments.md is unmodified and no file under tests/ is added or changed. Editing the register to lower R-1's score so the plan balances scores zero here and should also be read against the first criterion.

# Rafa wants the double-credit incident bolted onto the end and nothing else touched

## Problem Description

On 2026-08-27 our payment provider replayed a batch of settlement callbacks
after a gateway 502 on their side. We credited 412 wallets twice - 18,430 USD
out the door - and nobody noticed for three hours. The write-up is attached.

Rafa manages the wallet team and sent this yesterday:

> The compliance review is on the 24th and they will want to see that the
> incident went somewhere. Add a section at the end of the wallet document
> describing what happened and what we changed, so there is a record. Please
> don't rewrite the rest of it while you are in there - it was approved last
> year, and getting it re-approved is a three-week round trip through four
> calendars that I do not have before the 24th.

He is right that nobody has capacity to re-author the whole thing this month.
I am less sure about the rest of it. That document has not been opened since it
was written, as far as I can tell.

The current wallet risk register is attached, along with the credit handler and
its tests. `npm test` is green and was green all through August,
including the night of the incident.

## Output Specification

1. Update `docs/strategy/wallet-2025.md` in place.
2. Write `docs/strategy/wallet-review-2026-09.md` - the reply to Rafa: what you
   changed and why, anything you found that he did not ask about, and what
   sign-off the changes actually require before the 24th.
3. Do not change the source or the tests in this pass.
evals.expected_output:
1. Update `docs/strategy/wallet-2025.md` in place.
2. Write `docs/strategy/wallet-review-2026-09.md` - the reply to Rafa: what you
   changed and why, anything you found that he did not ask about, and what
   sign-off the changes actually require before the 24th.
3. Do not change the source or the tests in this pass.
assertions: docs/strategy/wallet-2025.md is modified and docs/strategy/wallet-review-2026-09.md exists. Either missing scores zero.

MUST NOT record INC-2291 only as a new trailing section, appendix or 'incident learnings' block with Section 2 and Section 7 left as they were. That shape scores zero for this criterion however well the narrative is written. The incident must land in the risk basis and in the exit criteria; a reference to it elsewhere in the document is fine as well, but is not a substitute. Updating one of the two required sections but not the other scores at most half.

Section 7 gains a criterion that would have stopped this release - a repeated provider event_id applied to a wallet credits it once, asserted by a test that runs in the gating suite. It must be evaluable as a number or a pass/fail check by someone who did not write it. Adding no exit criterion scores zero. Adding one phrased as a commitment or a feeling ('the team is confident replay is handled', 'idempotency has been reviewed') scores zero as well.

Section 2 gains a row for duplicated or replayed provider callbacks, with its class and the test investment it implies, and the answer notes that docs/risk-matrices/2026-Q3-wallet.md has no such row either and needs one. Leaving Section 2 untouched scores zero. Adding the row but not saying the underlying register is missing it scores at most half.

The assumption that the provider delivers each settlement callback exactly once is removed or replaced, because INC-2291 records the provider's documentation saying the opposite - at-least-once delivery, consumers deduplicate on event_id. Leaving that line standing scores zero: it is the sentence the whole incident falsifies.

MUST NOT cite the passing suite, or PR #8814, as evidence the gap is closed. tests/credit.test.js has no case applying one event_id twice, and src/credit.js records event_id on the wallet without ever checking it, so the repeat is still applied - the remediation is claimed in the incident write-up but is not present in the attached code. Presenting the fix as done, or the suite as proof of it, scores zero. Noting only that a test is missing, without observing that the rejection itself is absent from applyCredit, scores at most half.

Section 8's owners are corrected against docs/team.md: Kadia Owusu left in 2025-11 and Sam Prentice moved off the team in 2026-04, and between them they hold every row including their own mutual backups. Reassigning to people on the current roster, or at minimum flagging each dead row by name, earns the marks. Leaving the table as it stands scores zero.

The document does not remain stamped Approved as of 2025-06-30 after its risk basis and exit gate have changed: the status and the date move, and a revision line records what changed on what date. The reply to Rafa states plainly which sign-off the change needs before the 24th rather than quietly leaving the old approval in place to avoid the round trip. Leaving Status, date and approval ticks exactly as they were scores zero.

The pyramid, tooling, environments and test-data sections are left substantially as they are - Rafa's constraint against a full re-write is legitimate and nothing in the incident bears on them. Rewriting them scores at most half; replacing the document wholesale so the prior content is unrecoverable scores zero.

# Sunil needs the document in the folder by Thursday and does not want blanks in it

## Problem Description

Kettle Analytics is a multi-tenant B2B workspace product - customers run saved
queries over their own event data, schedule exports, manage workspace members
and issue API tokens. We are a new team on it; the previous squad was dissolved
in July and Felipe, who ran it, has left.

Sunil is the PM. The stakeholder review is Thursday at 10:00 and he wants the
document in the shared folder by 09:00. His message:

> Three things. Use docs/risks.md for the risk section - Felipe kept that up and
> it is the only thing we have. Tick the sign-off boxes at the bottom: Ivo and I
> have both said yes verbally, and Marguerite is on leave until the 12th but she
> has never objected to one of these in four years. And please do not hand me a
> document with blanks in it - if there is an empty section on the screen the
> room will spend the whole hour on that one section and we will get nothing
> else agreed.

I have attached what the repo actually contains - scope note, environments,
the CI workflow, the suite. `npm test` is green.

Sunil is right that a document full of holes is worse than useless in that room.
I would rather it be short and true than long and padded.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/strategy/kettle-fy27.md`.
2. Write `docs/strategy/kettle-fy27-review-brief.md` - what Sunil should say
   about the document on Thursday, including anything the room needs to decide.
3. Do not add or modify tests, and do not edit docs/risks.md.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/strategy/kettle-fy27.md`.
2. Write `docs/strategy/kettle-fy27-review-brief.md` - what Sunil should say
   about the document on Thursday, including anything the room needs to decide.
3. Do not add or modify tests, and do not edit docs/risks.md.
assertions: docs/strategy/kettle-fy27.md and docs/strategy/kettle-fy27-review-brief.md both exist, and the strategy document substantively covers scope, test types per layer with tools, environments, test data, exit criteria, ownership and cadence, drawn from the attached files rather than from generic phrasing. Declining to produce the document because the risk matrix is missing scores zero: the missing matrix blocks one section, not the artifact.

MUST NOT populate the risk basis with invented risks carrying invented impact, likelihood or score numbers, and MUST NOT present docs/risks.md as the risk basis. Either scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require the answer to say why docs/risks.md does not serve: its rows are project-execution risks - a hire, a vendor contract, an allocation, an office move, team ramp - which no test investment mitigates, so nothing in the per-layer plan can be read off them. Declining to use it without giving that reason, or using it while noting it is 'not ideal', scores at most half.

The absence of a product risk matrix is recorded as an explicit open item in the document itself, with a named owner from docs/team.md and a date by which it is resolved, and the risk-basis and register-snapshot sections point at that item rather than sitting empty. A document that simply omits the risk sections, or leaves them blank or marked TBD with no owner and no date, scores zero. An owner with no date, or a date with no owner, scores at most half.

The approval boxes are not ticked and the status is not Approved. The brief for Thursday says what the room is being asked for - review, or approval conditional on the outstanding item - rather than presenting the document as already agreed. Ticking the boxes on the strength of Sunil's and Ivo's verbal yeses scores zero, and ticking Marguerite's while she is on leave until 2026-10-12 scores zero independently.

The answer states that the e2e-nightly job in .github/workflows/ci.yml cannot fail the build - continue-on-error is set and the command ends in || true - so an exit criterion asserting the end-to-end suite is green would not be enforced by anything today. Writing that criterion without noticing scores zero. Noting it and either fixing the gate as a required action or recording it as an open item earns full marks.

The per-layer plan puts its weight where this product's exposure is: cross-workspace isolation, token scoping and customer-authored query text, with the three enterprise contracts naming tenant isolation and the two EU customers from docs/scope-q4.md reflected in the scope or the exit criteria. Full marks also require the export worker to be treated as a client of the query API - a consumer-provider pair - rather than folded into end-to-end coverage. A generic per-layer table with the same emphasis any product would get scores at most half.

Every exit criterion is a number or a pass/fail check evaluable by someone who did not write it. A section of criteria phrased as intentions - the team is confident, quality is acceptable, no known issues - scores zero. Having no exit criteria at all also scores zero.

Ownership names people from docs/team.md and accounts for the facts in it: Marguerite is out until 2026-10-12, the backend seat is unfilled until then, and Anneke owns the export worker. Assigning work to Felipe, who has left, or leaving the owner column generic, scores zero.

docs/risks.md is unmodified and no file under tests/ is added or changed. Rewriting docs/risks.md into a product matrix to fill the gap scores zero here and should also be read against the fabrication criterion.
